newsitem.title: FINLAND: Amer sees big units' 1997 profitability up.
newsitem.headline: Amer sees big units' 1997 profitability up.

text.p: Finnish loss-making sporting goods group Amer-yhtyma Oy said on Thursday it expected improving full-year profitability for its two biggest divisions while the third division's 1997 profitability would remain good.
For the whole group, Amer said 1997 earnings would improve significantly, but remain in the red. The consolidated 1996 loss before extraordinary items and tax was 234 million markka.
At its Wilson golf, racquet and team sport equipment unit, part of the sports division, "profitability is expected to improve significantly," Amer said in a statement with its January-April results.
Wilson's primary focus was on improving profitability rather than increasing sales, it said. The unit's full-year net sales were expected to remain unchanged compared to 1996.
Wilson's net sales of the first four months of 1997 grew eight percent to 1.48 billion markka. In full-year 1996, the unit's net sales were 2.82 billion markka.
Wilson's profitability improved in January-April, primarily due to aggressive cost cutting, Amer said. Profitability at the Atomic skiing equipment unit, is also expected to improve.
"Atomic is expected to strenghten its position in the ski market," Amer added.
But it predicted competition would become keener as new manufacturers enter the markets.
Atomic's net sales in the first four months of 1997 grew 17 percent to 184 million markka with branded product sales up 32 percent.
"Production problems at the ski factory, which affected 1996 results, have been eliminated," Amer said.
Amer said earnings at its Tobacco division were expected to improve compared to 1996 supported by higher sales and market share as well as price increases implemented in Finland.
In January-April, the tobacco division's net sales increased 53 percent to 144 million markka, boosted by higher delivery volumes and by a price increase at the beginning of the year.
The Time/system division's profitability would remain good and sales were expected to progress as planned this year, Amer said.
The division's net sales for the January-April period were 48 million markka, unchanged from the year-ago period.
"Sales of the PC based Time/system product Task/Timer 3.0 continued to grow. Competition continued to be keen," Amer said.
Amer's Jan-April loss more than halved to 49 million markka.
